sources.source_name: Marazzi Product Specifications — Italian Color Body Lines
sources.snippet: Marazzi Italian production: color body porcelain manufactured in Sassuolo, Italy (heart of Italian ceramics district since 1935). Color body construction — tinted body reduces chip visibility. Advanced digital inkjet printing technology from Italian press manufacturers (SACMI, System). Rectified edges. Water absorption <0.5% (porcelain grade). PEI Class 4. Available in multiple formats including 12x24, 24x24. Italian production maintains Sassuolo manufacturing standards distinct from Marazzi USA operations.
sources.classification_reason: Manufacturer specifications from Italian production facility.

sources.snippet: Marazzi Group acquired by Mohawk Industries in 2013. Founded 1935 in Sassuolo, Emilia-Romagna, Italy. Italian production lines continue to operate from Sassuolo facilities. US production (Marazzi USA) operates from separate facilities. The two production streams produce different products — Italian Marazzi maintains distinct clay body formulations, firing profiles, and quality standards from Marazzi USA lines.

Sassuolo, Italy is the world's leading ceramic manufacturing district. 200+ manufacturers within a 30km radius. 90+ years of continuous ceramic innovation. Advanced firing technology, proprietary clay body research, digital printing leadership. Italian tile has >40% global export share in premium segments. Marazzi is one of the founding names of the district, alongside Atlas Concorde, Florim, Iris Ceramica.
sources.classification_reason: Italian ceramics industry body — authoritative on manufacturing quality and heritage.

sources.source_name: Architect Specification — Italian vs US Marazzi
sources.snippet: Important distinction: Italian Marazzi and Marazzi USA are not the same product. Italian lines have tighter tolerances, richer color depth, and color body construction. US Marazzi (made in US Mohawk plants) uses standard white body and is positioned as mid-range. When I specify 'Marazzi' for a luxury project, I specifically call out Italian production. The price differential is 2-3x but the quality difference is visible.
sources.classification_reason: Professional architect with specific knowledge of Italian vs US Marazzi production differences.

sources.snippet: Italian Marazzi is a pleasure to work with. Beautiful color body, consistent sizing, cuts clean. The digital printing on their premium lines is some of the most realistic wood-look and stone-look I've seen. Very different from the Marazzi brand you find at Home Depot/Floor & Decor, which is US-made and more basic. If you can get genuine Italian Marazzi, it's excellent.
sources.classification_reason: Professional installer distinguishing between Italian and US production.

bottom_line: Italian-produced Marazzi color body porcelain represents the Sassuolo ceramic heritage — 90+ years of continuous manufacturing from the world's premier tile district. Color body construction, advanced digital inkjet, rectified edges, water absorption <0.5%. Now Mohawk-owned but Italian production maintains distinct quality standards from Marazzi USA. Professional consensus emphasizes the Italian vs US distinction: Italian lines have tighter tolerances, richer color, and color body construction that US lines lack. Excellent tile backed by both Italian heritage and Mohawk corporate stability.
